title: Sonata à la manière de Francis Poulenc
identity: Wijnand van Klaveren’s Sonate à la manière de Francis Poulenc (1998) is for alto saxophone and piano and is dedicated to Louis van Dijk. An Indiana University Doctor of Music dissertation analyzes all three movements and reproduces score excerpts. Its opening movement alternates Allegro and Paisiblement sections before returning to Allegro, with an ascending thirty-second-note saxophone pickup.

evidence.claim: Composer/publisher page gives instrumentation, date, competition use, and describes first-movement thematic construction.

Indiana University Doctor of Music dissertation identifies the 1998 alto saxophone and piano sonata, its dedication to Louis van Dijk, and analyzes its three movements; printed pp. 58–60 discuss first-movement sections and score examples.
evidence.source_name: Indiana University Jacobs School of Music dissertation

evidence.claim: Dissertation describes the opening saxophone gesture as an ascending seven-note thirty-second-note pickup and reproduces the opening score excerpt; the same motif recurs through the movement, including six appearances in piano.
evidence.source_name: Indiana University Jacobs School of Music dissertation

score_observations.claim: The dissertation's reproduced mm. 1–2 show an ascending thirty-second-note pickup in the alto saxophone part and continuous moving figures in the piano; the opening motif is passed between the instruments.

review_focus: Inference: the opening's rapid pickup and the documented exchange of its recurring motif with piano provide concrete points for reviewing articulation clarity and ensemble handoff.
collection_flag: Competition-listed college repertoire; no level proposed.

score_links.description: Institutional dissertation containing score examples, including first-movement mm. 1–2.

gaps: Dissertation analyzes score excerpts but is not a substitute for the complete score; full notation and recorded performance were not inspected.
The dissertation lists optional semifinal use in the 2023 Adolphe Sax Competition; current competition repertoire status is not established.
